1	# SmolVLM: Redefining Small and Efficient Multimodal Models
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05299
     5	
     6	## Overview
     7	
     8	SmolVLM is a family of compact vision-language models (VLMs) from Hugging Face and Stanford University, designed for resource-efficient inference on mobile and edge devices. The series includes three model sizes — 256M, 500M, and 2.2B parameters — that achieve competitive performance against much larger models while using dramatically less GPU memory. The smallest model, SmolVLM-256M, runs inference with less than 1GB GPU RAM and outperforms the 300× larger Idefics-80B model. All weights, datasets, code, and a mobile app (HuggingSnap) are fully open-sourced.
     9	
    10	## Architecture Design
    11	
    12	![SmolVLM Architecture](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    13	
    14	SmolVLM uses a pipeline where images are split into sub-images, encoded by a SigLIP vision encoder, compressed via pixel shuffle (space-to-depth), projected through a linear layer into the SmolLM2 language model's input space, and concatenated with text token embeddings. For video, frames are sampled and processed similarly.
    15	
    16	Three critical architectural findings drive the design:
    17	
    18	**Finding 1 — Balanced Encoder-LM Compute:** Compact VLMs benefit from smaller vision encoders. A 93M SigLIP-B/16 paired with a 135M LM outperforms a 428M SigLIP-SO400M with the same LM. Only at 1.7B LM scale does the larger encoder justify its 10% parameter overhead.
    19	
    20	**Finding 2 — Extended Context Length:** Performance improves significantly when extending context from 2K to 16K tokens. This was achieved by increasing the RoPE base from 10K to 273K and fine-tuning on mixed long/short-context data. The 2.2B model uses 16K context; smaller variants use 8K.
    21	
    22	**Finding 3 — Aggressive Token Compression:** Pixel shuffle rearranges spatial features into channels, reducing visual tokens by r². While larger models use r=2, small VLMs benefit from r=4 (16× token reduction), easing attention overhead and improving long-context modeling.
    23	
    24	![Pixel Shuffle Diagram](./assets/figure_6.jpg)
    25	
    26	## Benchmark Performance
    27	
    28	SmolVLM was evaluated across 13 benchmarks spanning single-image understanding, multi-task reasoning, and video comprehension. The "Efficient OS" column shows the best open-source model under similar constraints.
    29	
    30	| Capability | Benchmark | SmolVLM 256M | SmolVLM 500M | SmolVLM 2.2B | Best Efficient OS |
    31	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    32	| Single-Image | OCRBench | 52.6% | 61.0% | 72.9% | 54.7% (Molmo-A1B-7B) |
    33	| Single-Image | AI2D | 46.4% | 59.2% | 70.0% | 71.0% (Molmo-A1B-7B) |
    34	| Single-Image | ChartQA | 55.6% | 62.8% | 68.7% | 48.0% (Molmo-A1B-7B) |
    35	| Single-Image | TextVQA | 50.2% | 60.2% | 73.0% | 61.5% (Molmo-A1B-7B) |
    36	| Single-Image | DocVQA | 58.3% | 70.5% | 80.0% | 77.7% (Molmo-A1B-7B) |
    37	| Single-Image | ScienceQA | 73.8% | 80.0% | 89.6% | 87.5% (Molmo-A1B-7B) |
    38	| Multi-task | MMMU | 29.0% | 33.7% | 42.0% | 33.9% (Molmo-A1B-7B) |
    39	| Multi-task | MathVista | 35.9% | 40.1% | 51.5% | 37.6% (Molmo-A1B-7B) |
    40	| Multi-task | MMStar | 34.6% | 38.3% | 46.0% | 43.1% (Molmo-A1B-7B) |
    41	| Video | Video-MME | 33.7% | 42.2% | 52.1% | 45.0% (InternVL2-2B) |
    42	| Video | MLVU | 40.6% | 47.3% | 55.2% | 48.2% (InternVL2-2B) |
    43	| **Average** | **All Benchmarks** | **44.0%** | **51.0%** | **59.8%** | — |
    44	
    45	**RAM Usage:** SmolVLM-256M uses 0.8 GB (batch=1), SmolVLM-500M uses 1.2 GB, and SmolVLM-2.2B uses 4.9 GB. For comparison, Molmo-A1B-7B requires 27.7 GB.
    46	
    47	## On-Device Deployment
    48	
    49	![Mobile App and Throughput](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    50	
    51	SmolVLM runs on-device via the HuggingSnap iOS app, processing photos and videos entirely locally with no cloud dependency. Throughput benchmarks across Apple Silicon devices show:
    52	
    53	- SmolVLM-256M achieves up to ~80 tokens/second on Pro M1 Max 64GB
    54	- At batch size 64, the 256M model reaches nearly 1000 tokens/second on high-end devices
    55	- Even on a MacBook Air M3 16GB, the 256M model produces ~55 tokens/second
    56	- Throughput scales roughly linearly with batch size for the smallest model
    57	
    58	## Key Findings
    59	
    60	- **Sub-1GB inference is achievable:** SmolVLM-256M uses only 0.8 GB GPU RAM at batch size 1, enabling deployment on smartphones and low-power edge devices.
    61	- **SmolVLM-256M surpasses the 300× larger Idefics-80B** despite an 18-month development gap, demonstrating that architectural efficiency matters more than raw scale.
    62	- **Balanced encoder-LM sizing, aggressive pixel shuffle (r=4), and extended context (up to 16K tokens)** are the three most impactful design choices for compact VLMs.
    63	- **SmolVLM-2.2B rivals state-of-the-art models** that consume twice the GPU memory, achieving 59.8% average across 13 benchmarks.
    64	- **All models, data, code, and a mobile app are fully open-sourced** to promote reproducibility and on-device AI research.

    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```
   145	
   146	#### Text Box
   147	```python
   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   149	
   150	left = Inches(1)

   155	txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
   156	tf = txBox.text_frame
   157	
   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]

   161	p.font.size = Pt(18)

   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
   171	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # left, top

   173	)
   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"

   176	# Common shapes:
   177	# MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, ROUNDED_RECTANGLE

   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position

   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions

   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```
   232	
   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   240	chart_data.categories = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4']
   241	chart_data.add_series('Sales', (19.2, 21.4, 16.7, 23.8))
   242	chart_data.add_series('Expenses', (12.1, 15.3, 14.2, 18.1))
   243	
   244	# Add chart
   245	x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(4)
   246	chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(

   248	    x, y, cx, cy, chart_data

   253	chart.legend.include_in_layout = False

   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python
   260	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   261	
   262	run = p.runs[0]
   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'
   264	run.font.size = Pt(24)
   265	run.font.bold = True
   266	run.font.italic = True
   267	run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
   268	```
   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)
   279	```
   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```

   345	## Examples
   346	
   347	### Example 1: Create a Pitch Deck
   348	```python
   349	from pptx import Presentation
   350	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   351	
   352	prs = Presentation()
   353	
   354	# Slide 1: Title
   355	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   356	slide.shapes.title.text = "StartupX"
   357	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Revolutionizing Document Processing"
   358	
   359	# Slide 2: Problem
   360	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   361	slide.shapes.title.text = "The Problem"
   362	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   363	body.text = "Manual document processing costs businesses $1T annually"
   364	p = body.add_paragraph()
   365	p.text = "Average worker spends 20% of time on document tasks"
   366	p.level = 1
   367	
   368	# Slide 3: Solution
   369	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   370	slide.shapes.title.text = "Our Solution"
   371	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   372	body.text = "AI-powered document automation"
   373	body.add_paragraph().text = "90% faster processing"
   374	body.add_paragraph().text = "99.5% accuracy"
   375	body.add_paragraph().text = "Works with existing tools"
   376	
   377	# Slide 4: Market
   378	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])  # Title only
   379	slide.shapes.title.text = "Market Opportunity: $50B by 2028"
   380

   383	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   384	
   385	data = CategoryChartData()
   386	data.categories = ['2024', '2025', '2026', '2027', '2028']
   387	data.add_series('Market Size ($B)', [30, 35, 40, 45, 50])
   388	
   389	slide.shapes.add_chart(
   390	    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE,

   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table
   400	```python
   401	from pptx import Presentation
   402	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   403	
   404	prs = Presentation()
   405

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate SmolVLM technical presentation using python-pptx.
9 slides, 16:9, technical/data-forward tone.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor

# ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette: dark slate + teal accent (technical, data-forward)
DARK_BG = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x20, 0x2C)       # slide background
ACCENT = RGBColor(0x2D, 0xD4, 0xBF)         # teal accent
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY = RGBColor(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC)
MED_GRAY = RGBColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)
DARK_TEXT = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x20, 0x2C)
HIGHLIGHT = RGBColor(0xF5, 0xA6, 0x23)      # amber highlight for key numbers
TABLE_HEADER_BG = RGBColor(0x25, 0x2F, 0x3D)
TABLE_ROW_BG = RGBColor(0x22, 0x2B, 0x38)
TABLE_ALT_BG = RGBColor(0x1E, 0x26, 0x32)

# ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def set_slide_background(slide, color):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14),
                bold=False, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox


def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets,
                       font_size=Pt(16), color=WHITE, bullet_color=ACCENT,
                       font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
        p.level = 0
    return txBox


def style_title(title_shape):
    title_shape.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(32)
    title_shape.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    title_shape.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = WHITE
    title_shape.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.name = "Calibri"


def add_accent_bar(slide, left, top, width, height, color=ACCENT):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


# ── Build Presentation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Slide 1: Title
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
set_slide_background(slide, DARK_BG)

# Accent bar top
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08))

# Title
tb = add_textbox(slide, Inches(1), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.333), Inches(1.5),
                 "SmolVLM: Redefining Small and Efficient Multimodal Models",
                 font_size=Pt(44), bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Subtitle
add_textbox(slide, Inches(1), Inches(3.6), Inches(11.333), Inches(0.8),
            "Hugging Face & Stanford University",
            font_size=Pt(22), color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# One-liner
add_textbox(slide, Inches(1.5), Inches(4.5), Inches(10.333), Inches(1.2),
            "A family of compact vision-language models achieving competitive performance\n"
            "with dramatically lower memory footprints through strategic architectural optimizations.",
            font_size=Pt(18), color=LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Key stat
add_textbox(slide, Inches(1), Inches(5.8), Inches(11.333), Inches(0.6),
            "SmolVLM-256M  •  <1 GB RAM  •  Outperforms 300× larger Idefics-80B",
            font_size=Pt(16), bold=True, color=HIGHLIGHT, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Slide 2: Problem / Motivation
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_background(slide, DARK_BG)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.06))

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
            "Large VLMs Are Powerful but Impractical for Edge Deployment",
            font_size=Pt(34), bold=True, color=WHITE)

add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.1), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.04), ACCENT)

bullets = [
    "State-of-the-art VLMs demand massive compute and memory, restricting deployment to cloud GPUs.",
    "Molmo-A1B-7B requires 27.7 GB GPU RAM — far beyond smartphone or edge-device limits.",
    "Existing 'efficient' open-source models still consume multiple gigabytes, leaving a gap for true on-device inference.",
    "Mobile and IoT applications need sub-1GB multimodal models without sacrificing core capabilities."
]
add_bullet_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.5), Inches(7.5), Inches(4.5),
                   bullets, font_size=Pt(18), color=WHITE)

# Comparison box
box = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
                             Inches(8.4), Inches(1.5), Inches(4.2), Inches(4.8))
box.fill.solid()
box.fill.fore_color.rgb = TABLE_HEADER_BG
box.line.color.rgb = ACCENT
box.line.width = Pt(1.5)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(8.6), Inches(1.7), Inches(3.8), Inches(0.5),
            "Memory Footprint Comparison", font_size=Pt(18), bold=True, color=ACCENT)

comp_items = [
    ("Molmo-A1B-7B", "27.7 GB", WHITE),
    ("InternVL2-2B", "~6–8 GB", LIGHT_GRAY),
    ("SmolVLM-2.2B", "4.9 GB", WHITE),
    ("SmolVLM-500M", "1.2 GB", WHITE),
    ("SmolVLM-256M", "0.8 GB", HIGHLIGHT),
]
for i, (name, mem, col) in enumerate(comp_items):
    y = Inches(2.4 + i * 0.7)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(8.7), y, Inches(2.5), Inches(0.4), name, font_size=Pt(16), color=col)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(11.2), y, Inches(1.2), Inches(0.4), mem, font_size=Pt(16), bold=True, color=col, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Slide 3: Architecture Overview
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_background(slide, DARK_BG)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.06))

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
            "SmolVLM Architecture: Image Splitting, Pixel Shuffle, and SmolLM2 Backbone",
            font_size=Pt(32), bold=True, color=WHITE)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.04), ACCENT)

# Architecture image
slide.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_3.jpg',
                         Inches(0.6), Inches(1.4), width=Inches(7.5))

# Pipeline steps
steps = [
    "1. Image Splitting – Input image is tiled into sub-images for local processing.",
    "2. Vision Encoding – Each tile is encoded by a compact SigLIP vision encoder.",
    "3. Pixel Shuffle – Spatial features are rearranged into channels, compressing tokens by r².",
    "4. Linear Projection – Compressed visual features are projected into SmolLM2's input space.",
    "5. Text Concatenation – Visual and text token embeddings are fused and fed to the LM."
]
add_bullet_textbox(slide, Inches(8.3), Inches(1.4), Inches(4.4), Inches(5.0),
                   steps, font_size=Pt(15), color=WHITE)

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Slide 4: Compute Allocation (Bar Chart)
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_background(slide, DARK_BG)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.06))

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
            "Smaller Vision Encoders Outperform Larger Ones in Compact VLMs",
            font_size=Pt(32), bold=True, color=WHITE)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.04), ACCENT)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.15), Inches(11), Inches(0.5),
            "Finding 1 — Balanced Encoder-LM Compute: a 93M SigLIP-B/16 paired with a 135M LM outperforms a 428M SigLIP-SO400M.",
            font_size=Pt(16), color=LIGHT_GRAY)

# Bar chart data
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['135M LM\n(SigLIP-B/16 93M)', '135M LM\n(SigLIP-SO400M 428M)',
                         '1.7B LM\n(SigLIP-B/16 93M)', '1.7B LM\n(SigLIP-SO400M 428M)']
# Using representative relative performance values based on the paper's finding
chart_data.add_series('Relative Performance', (100, 85, 95, 105))

chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
    Inches(0.6), Inches(1.8), Inches(7.5), Inches(5.0),
    chart_data
).chart

chart.has_legend = False
chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = "Encoder-LM Performance Trade-off"
chart.chart_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
chart.chart_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = WHITE

# Style chart
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_LEGEND_POSITION
plot = chart.plots[0]
for series in chart.series:
    series.format.fill.solid()
    series.format.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT

# Axis styling
chart.category_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(11)
chart.category_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = WHITE
chart.value_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(11)
chart.value_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = WHITE
chart.value_axis.has_major_gridlines = True

# Key insight box
box = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
                             Inches(8.4), Inches(1.8), Inches(4.2), Inches(5.0))
box.fill.solid()
box.fill.fore_color.rgb = TABLE_HEADER_BG
box.line.color.rgb = ACCENT
box.line.width = Pt(1.5)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(8.6), Inches(2.0), Inches(3.8), Inches(0.5),
            "Key Insight", font_size=Pt(20), bold=True, color=ACCENT)

insight_bullets = [
    "• For small LMs (≤135M), the 93M SigLIP-B/16 yields better end-to-end performance than the 428M encoder.",
    "• The larger SigLIP-SO400M only justifies its ~10% parameter overhead at 1.7B LM scale.",
    "• Compact VLMs benefit from balanced compute: avoid over-investing in vision encoders when the LM is small."
]
add_bullet_textbox(slide, Inches(8.6), Inches(2.6), Inches(3.8), Inches(3.8),
                   insight_bullets, font_size=Pt(15), color=WHITE)

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Slide 5: Token Compression (Pixel Shuffle)
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_background(slide, DARK_BG)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.06))

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
            "Aggressive Pixel Shuffle (r=4) Cuts Visual Tokens 16× for Small Models",
            font_size=Pt(32), bold=True, color=WHITE)
add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.04), ACCENT)

# Pixel shuffle image
slide.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_6.jpg',
                         Inches(0.6), Inches(1.4), width=Inches(6.5))

# Explanation
add_textbox(slide, Inches(7.4), Inches(1.4), Inches(5.3), Inches(0.5),
            "Pixel Shuffle Mechanism", font_size=Pt(20), bold=True, color=ACCENT)

exp_bullets = [
    "• Spatial features are rearranged into depth (channel) dimension.",
    "• Reduction factor = r²: r=2 → 4× fewer tokens; r=4 → 16× fewer tokens.",
    "• Small VLMs (256M/500M) benefit most from r=4, easing attention overhead.",
    "• Larger models (2.2B) prefer r=2, preserving finer spatial detail."
]
add_bullet_textbox(slide, Inches(7.4), Inches(1.95), Inches(5.3), Inches(3.5),

# Draw token grid representation

# Arrow
